name: Hilary Shane
current_role: Private investor; >5% / 10% beneficial owner of FONAR Corp (FONR) via a revocable trust
profile: Hilary L. Shane is a private investor who has accumulated a large stake in MRI company FONAR Corp; a January 2026 Schedule 13G (filed as a passive investor) reported ~6.66% of FONAR's common stock, and Form 4s show continued open-market purchases in 2026. No public biography or operating role found.
interesting_fact: Her FONAR holdings are reported through the Hilary L. Shane Revocable Trust and filed on a passive basis, stating the shares are not held to influence control of the company.
notes: Very private individual investor; no public profile, website or social accounts found. Only public trace is SEC filings (EDGAR CIK filings for FONR). Identity beyond the filings could not be confirmed. Not a fit for outreach without a warm intro.

name: Lois K Zabrocky
current_role: President & CEO and Director, International Seaways, Inc. (NYSE: INSW); Director, Tidewater Inc.
profile: Lois Zabrocky has been the first and only CEO of International Seaways, one of the largest US-listed tanker owners, since its 2016 spin-off from Overseas Shipholding Group, where she spent ~25 years and ran the International Flag unit. She also sits on the boards of Tidewater, BIMCO and ITOPF.
interesting_fact: She is one of very few women leading a major listed tanker company, and her whole 30+ year career has been with INSW and its predecessor OSG.
deep_cut_fact: She began her career at sea: a graduate of the US Merchant Marine Academy holding a Third Mate's license, she sailed as third mate on a chemical tanker in the US Jones Act fleet before moving ashore.
notes: Frequent speaker at Capital Link and Marine Money shipping forums — conference circuit is a natural route. IR/media contact is Tom Trovato (Investor Relations & Media) per company press releases.

name: Vidyadhara K Gubbi
current_role: Chief of Global Operations, Western Digital (WD) (since Feb 2025)
profile: Vidya Gubbi runs Western Digital's global operations — manufacturing, procurement, supply chain, quality, sustainability and real estate — across 35,000+ employees. A 38-year storage-industry veteran with ~20 years at WD, he previously led WD's Hard Disk Drive Operating Unit; his wealth comes from WD equity as HDD demand surged with AI data-center build-outs.
interesting_fact: He sits on the Board of Directors of the Global Semiconductor Alliance and oversees the factories producing the high-capacity hard drives that hyperscale AI data centers rely on.
deep_cut_fact: Before WD he held senior roles at Maxtor and Seagate, is a named inventor on multiple hard-disk-drive patents, and trained as a mechanical engineer (BS from India's National Institute of Technology, MS from Santa Clara University).
notes: Low public profile operations executive; strong data-center angle (HDD supply for AI storage). Route via WD corporate media inquiries.

name: Bruce A Kiefer
current_role: Independent Director, Mid Penn Bancorp (NASDAQ: MPB) since March 2023; chemist at The Hershey Company
profile: Bruce Kiefer is a long-serving Hershey Company chemist (since 1984) who joined the board of Pennsylvania bank holding company Mid Penn Bancorp in March 2023. SEC filings show him as a substantial Mid Penn shareholder (roughly 1 million shares per third-party trackers), which drives his listed net worth.
interesting_fact: At Hershey he oversees the Laboratory Information Management System database and serves as the company's Chemical Hygiene Officer.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a chemistry degree from Dickinson College and a master's in food science from Penn State, is an avid cyclist, and volunteers tutoring high school students in math and science.
notes: Low public profile; not a founder/operator. Only route is via Mid Penn Bancorp corporate/IR. Source of his large share stake not publicly explained — do not speculate.

name: John W Kosiba Jr
current_role: Senior Vice President, CFO & Treasurer, American Superconductor Corp. (AMSC) (since April 2017)
profile: John Kosiba has been CFO of AMSC — the Massachusetts maker of grid, wind and Navy power-electronics and superconductor systems — since 2017, after joining in 2010 to run finance operations and later the Gridtec solutions business. His wealth reflects AMSC's sharp stock rebound on grid/data-center power demand.
interesting_fact: Before becoming CFO he ran AMSC's Gridtec solutions business (grid-stabilisation products) alongside finance operations — unusual operating experience for a CFO at a power-technology company.
deep_cut_fact: Before AMSC he was division director and controller at Amphenol Aerospace, a division of Amphenol Corp., overseeing the division's finance, budgeting and audit; he joined AMSC in June 2010 as managing director of finance operations.
notes: Strong energy/grid angle (AMSC supplies grid power-quality and superconductor systems). Media contact is AMSC Director of Communications Nicol Golez; IR via Alliance Advisors.

name: Keith Woods
current_role: Chief Operating Officer, Scholar Rock (NASDAQ: SRRK) since April 2025; Director, X4 Pharmaceuticals
profile: R. Keith Woods is a 30-year biopharma commercial operator who joined Scholar Rock as COO in April 2025 to build global commercial operations for its SMA drug apitegromab. He was previously COO of argenx, where he helped build the commercial organisation for Vyvgart, and earlier held senior roles at Alexion, Roche, Amgen and Eisai.
interesting_fact: After leaving argenx as COO he stayed on as an advisor to the argenx board; he also sits on the boards of Neurogene and X4 Pharmaceuticals.
deep_cut_fact: Before argenx he was Vice President and Managing Director of Alexion UK, after serving as Alexion's SVP of North American Operations; he holds a BS in marketing from Florida State University.
notes: Biotech executive — weak fit for an energy/data-center podcast but fits entrepreneurship/scale-up angle. Route via Scholar Rock media team.

name: Michael P Connors
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, Information Services Group (NASDAQ: III); Lead Director, Chubb Ltd.
profile: Mike Connors founded ISG in 2006 (IPO'd as a SPAC in 2007) and built it into a global technology research and advisory firm that advises enterprises on sourcing, cloud and AI. Earlier he was Chairman/CEO of VNU's Media Measurement & Information group (now Nielsen) and Vice Chairman of ACNielsen. He is also Lead Director of insurer Chubb.
interesting_fact: As Vice Chairman of ACNielsen he helped grow its equity value from $893M at its 1996 spin-off from Dun & Bradstreet to $2.3B when sold to VNU in 2001; in 2001 he formed VNU's MMI group combining Nielsen Media Research, NetRatings and Nielsen Entertainment.
deep_cut_fact: As a D&B senior vice president he played a leading role in splitting Dun & Bradstreet into three publicly traded companies in 1996, and he later chaired VNU World Directories, a Yellow Pages business in seven countries.
notes: ISG's research on AI, cloud and data-center sourcing fits the podcast; Connors has done CNBC appearances (Power Lunch, Fast Money), so media-comfortable. Route via ISG press team or Matter Communications.

name: John Smith Clark Ii
current_role: Co-Founder & Co-Portfolio Manager, Southpoint Capital Advisors LP (New York long/short equity hedge fund)
profile: John S. Clark II co-founded Southpoint Capital Advisors in March 2004, a New York-based, value-oriented long/short equity hedge fund. His 10%-owner position in Fennec Pharmaceuticals (FENC) is held through Southpoint entities, of which he is managing member; filings show large FENC sales in late 2025.
interesting_fact: Southpoint is a bottom-up, value-oriented long/short fund that has publicly disclosed both long and short positions (e.g. long Twitter and Carvana, short the S&P and railroads in investor letters).
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Southpoint he was an analyst at David Einhorn's Greenlight Capital; he graduated from UNC Chapel Hill in 1995 and earned an MBA with distinction from Harvard Business School in 2002.
notes: Private hedge-fund manager with very low public profile; no official website, press contact or social accounts found. Best route would be a warm intro via the hedge-fund community.

name: Ian Brady
current_role: Executive Fellow, Harvard Business School (2025–26); Solo GP, Prestwick Ventures; SoFi co-founder
profile: Ian Brady co-founded SoFi in 2011 with three fellow Stanford GSB students, pioneering alumni-funded student-loan refinancing. He later co-founded and led AI nutrition startup AVA (acquired by DSM in 2019) and then Hologram Sciences, and is now an Executive Fellow at Harvard Business School and an angel investor via Prestwick Ventures.
interesting_fact: SoFi grew out of a Stanford GSB idea of having alumni fund lower-rate loans for current students — the four co-founders met there.
deep_cut_fact: His undergraduate degree is a BA in Art History from Syracuse University; before SoFi he worked in investment banking and was Director of Innovation at Fidelity Investments, then studied at Stanford GSB as a Sloan Fellow.
notes: Hurun listing reflects SoFi founder status; no longer at SoFi and per reports co-founders no longer hold meaningful stakes. Good entrepreneurship-arc guest (SoFi -> AVA exit -> Hologram Sciences -> HBS). LinkedIn is the best direct route.

name: Charles A. Taylor
current_role: W.A. 'Tex' Moncrief Jr. Chair in Computational Medicine, Oden Institute, UT Austin & Professor, Dell Medical School; HeartFlow co-founder and director
profile: Charley Taylor is a computational-biomechanics pioneer who co-founded HeartFlow (2007 as Cardiovascular Simulation), which turns CT scans into AI-driven 3D blood-flow models of the heart; he was its CTO 2010–2021 and CSO 2021–2023, and HeartFlow listed on Nasdaq in 2025. Since 2025 he leads UT Austin's new Center for Computational Medicine.
interesting_fact: He was elected to the National Academy of Engineering in 2024 and is credited with more than 300 issued or pending patents.
deep_cut_fact: He earned three degrees at RPI (BS Mech. Eng. 1987, MS Mech. Eng. 1991, MS Mathematics 1992) before a Stanford PhD, and ran the first computer simulations of blood flow in patient-specific models built from medical imaging data.
notes: Academic-founder; HeartFlow is heavy AI/compute user (digital twins). Best route is via UT Austin Oden Institute / Dell Med communications, or HeartFlow media contact (Elliot Levy). Sources differ on his current HeartFlow title (some list CTO/director).

name: Dmitri Gaskin
current_role: Co-founder, Branch (Branch Metrics, mobile deep-linking); current title unclear — previously Head of Engineering
profile: Dmitri Gaskin co-founded Branch in 2014 with Alex Austin, Mada Seghete and Mike Molinet at age 19, building the deep-linking platform that routes users to specific pages inside mobile apps; Branch reached a ~$4B valuation in 2022. He led engineering in the early years. No recent public activity found.
interesting_fact: As a teenager (age 14) he was already a notable Drupal core contributor, helping lead the brainstorming session on the block-system overhaul for Drupal 8.
deep_cut_fact: As a teenage Drupal core contributor (handle dmitrig01), Google's Open Source team sponsored him to attend DrupalCon DC 2009, where he presented a session on jQuery; his Drupal.org profile also called him an award-winning composer and Steve Reich fan.
notes: Very low public profile; not on Branch's current leadership page, so current role is unverified ('alive' marked unknown only because no recent activity was found — no indication otherwise). Branch contact form is a weak route; a warm intro via Branch co-founders may work better.

name: Guilherme Bonifacio
current_role: Angel investor and serial entrepreneur (iFood co-founder; co-founder of Mercê do Bairro)
profile: Guilherme Bonifácio is one of four co-founders of iFood (2011), Brazil's dominant food-delivery app, which grew out of the phone-and-fax ordering service Disk Cook. He later ran sister company Rapiddo, was the last founder to sell his iFood stake, and has since co-founded neighbourhood-commerce startup Mercê do Bairro and invests in pre-seed/seed startups.
interesting_fact: iFood began as Disk Cook, which ran on a printed menu magazine, orders by phone and fax, and motorcycle couriers before splitting into the iFood marketplace in 2011.
deep_cut_fact: Before iFood he worked in Belgium as a consultant for brewer InBev, leaving that executive track to start his own company with college friends.
notes: Brazil-based (São Paulo); Portuguese-language outreach recommended. No published email or official site found; LinkedIn likely the best route but not verified. Co-founded Mercê do Bairro with Zé Delivery co-founder Diego Libanio (per a 2022 profile).

name: Shen Peng
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, Waterdrop Inc. (Shuidi, NYSE: WDH)
profile: Shen Peng joined Meituan around 2010 as roughly its 10th employee and helped launch and lead Meituan Waimai, its food-delivery business. In 2016 he founded Waterdrop (Shuidi), a medical crowdfunding and insurance-distribution platform aimed at under-insured Chinese families, and took it public on the NYSE in 2021; he continues to lead it as CEO.
interesting_fact: The idea for Waterdrop came after he organised a company-wide donation drive at Meituan when a delivery rider's mother needed brain-tumour surgery; he left to found the company that same year.
deep_cut_fact: He started at Meituan as a customer-service intern (billed as Meituan's first intern) and in 2013 led the team that launched Meituan's food-delivery platform as an internal venture; he likens a strong first employer to 'riding a rocket' (坐上火箭).
notes: China-based (Beijing); Mandarin outreach advised. Named to Hurun U40 China lists (2025, 2026); has a World Economic Forum profile. Best route is Waterdrop IR.

name: Jessica Lam
current_role: Technical/product advisor and seed investor; early Notion co-founder (self-described)
profile: Jessica Lam is a software architect and serial entrepreneur who joined Notion as a co-founder in 2014 when Notion acquired the collaboration-tools startup she had founded with a former Apple colleague, working on backend services, permissions and universal search. She later led engineering at LoungeBuddy (acquired by American Express) and now advises and invests in pre-seed/seed startups.
interesting_fact: Before Notion she was a senior software engineer at Apple, and later was Chief Architect/VP Engineering at airport-lounge app LoungeBuddy through its acquisition by American Express.
deep_cut_fact: She is also an oil painter, and earlier at Sony Pictures Interactive she pioneered the studio's iOS development, building one of its early iPad apps.
notes: Input name 'and Jessica Lam' is a parsing artifact. Her co-founder credit is self-reported (Wellfound, Elpha AMA); Notion's commonly cited co-founders are Ivan Zhao and Simon Last, so treat the Hurun listing cautiously. Any Notion equity is not public.

name: Arik Shtilman
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Rapyd (global fintech-as-a-service / payments platform)
profile: Arik Shtilman co-founded Rapyd in 2016 with Arkady Karpman and Omer Priel and built it into one of Israel's first fintech decacorns, offering payments, payouts and local payment-method APIs across 100+ countries. Before Rapyd he bootstrapped ITNavigator, a communications integrator and cloud contact-centre platform acquired by Avaya in 2013.
interesting_fact: His first company, ITNavigator, was bootstrapped in 2004 and grew to multimillion-dollar revenue before Avaya bought it in 2013; he and his co-founders then worked at Avaya for two years before starting Rapyd.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a BSc in Computer Science from the Interdisciplinary Center (IDC) Herzliya, and founded ITNavigator after three years of military service, focusing early on cloud computing.
notes: Israel/London-based; frequent fintech-conference speaker (Money20/20, Paris Fintech Forum, London Tech Week) and has done founder podcasts (e.g. Alejandro Cremades), so receptive to podcast format. Clarity PR address came from a Dubai-expansion release; confirm current agency on rapyd.net press page.

name: Huang Xiaohuang
current_role: Co-founder & Chairman, Manycore Tech (群核科技, HKEX-listed April 2026; maker of Kujiale and Coohom)
profile: Huang Xiaohuang (Victor Huang) co-founded Hangzhou-based Manycore in 2013 with Chen Hang and Zhu Hao, building cloud 3D design/rendering software (Kujiale, overseas Coohom) for home renovation and interiors. Manycore listed in Hong Kong in April 2026, the first of Hangzhou's 'six little dragons' to go public, and he is steering it toward spatial intelligence and robot-training data.
interesting_fact: Manycore now sells simulated 3D spatial data to train robots (customers include Agibot) and has open-sourced spatial-AI models SpatialLM and SpatialGen; Huang says robotics is 'poised to be the next real estate'.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Manycore he worked on Nvidia's CUDA team in the US (after a Zhejiang University undergrad and a UIUC graduate degree), returning to China in 2011 because 'the economy in the U.S. wasn't doing well... but in China, real estate was booming.'
notes: Strong GPU/compute angle (ex-Nvidia CUDA engineer, GPU cloud-rendering company, spatial AI). China-based; Mandarin outreach advised. No published press/IR email found in this pass — check Manycore's HKEX investor-relations page. Web search budget ran out before contacts could be researched further.

name: Soul Htite
current_role: Serial fintech founder (LendingClub co-founder, Dianrong founder; listed by Hurun as Upgrade co-founder); current role unverified
profile: Soul (Soulaiman) Htite was an original co-founder and technology lead/CTO of LendingClub, leading design and development of its online lending platform. In 2012 he moved to China and co-founded Dianrong, dubbed the 'Lending Club of China', serving as CEO until 2017; Hurun lists him among founders of US neobank Upgrade (Renaud Laplanche's company).
interesting_fact: In 2012 he moved from the US to China, teamed up with Shanghai finance lawyer Kevin Guo and founded Dianrong, which grew to 3,500+ employees and was nicknamed the 'Lending Club of China'.
deep_cut_fact: His one-line take on US vs China P2P lending: in the US it cut a borrower's rate by 4-5 points, whereas in China it was 'about building an infrastructure that did not exist before' — giving loans to people who previously couldn't get them.
notes: Upgrade link is from Hurun/MarketScreener only; he is not named on Upgrade's site, so the Upgrade press address is a weak route. Web search budget ran out before his current role could be confirmed. Avoid Dianrong's later history in outreach.

name: Victor Faramond
profile: Victor Faramond is a French engineer who co-founded crypto payments company MoonPay with Ivan Soto-Wright (and Maximilian Crown), launching its fiat-to-crypto on-ramp in 2019. MoonPay reached a $3.4B valuation in 2021–22 and now serves users in ~160 countries; he moved from CTO to Chief Engineer in 2022.
interesting_fact: MoonPay's first partnership, with Bitcoin.com, was signed in Tokyo about six months before launch — 'We basically had a contract before even building the final product,' Faramond said.
deep_cut_fact: MoonPay's origin story casts the two founders as opposites — Soto-Wright 'the idealist' and Faramond 'the grounded realist' — and the company debuted its minimum viable product in Tokyo in March 2019.
notes: Low-profile technical co-founder; CEO Ivan Soto-Wright is MoonPay's public face. Route via MoonPay media team.

name: Roger Van Duinen
profile: Listed by Hurun as a founder of Varo Bank (neobank; ~$2B valuation). Varo's public records (Wikipedia) name Colin Walsh as founder (2015); no public source found in this pass linking Roger Van Duinen to Varo or describing his role.
notes: Could not confirm identity — the Hurun founder attribution may be erroneous or refer to an early team member. Web search budget ran out before further checks; needs a follow-up search before any outreach.

name: Dmitriy Karpman
current_role: Co-founder, Hive (thehive.ai, AI content-moderation and deepfake-detection APIs); historically CTO
profile: Dmitriy Karpman co-founded San Francisco AI company Hive with CEO Kevin Guo; Hive sells cloud-hosted ML models via API for content moderation, AI-generated-content and deepfake detection, trained with data labelled by ~700,000 gig workers on its Hive Work app. Hive raised $85M at a $2B valuation in April 2021.
interesting_fact: Hive built its training-data pipeline on a crowd workforce of around 700,000 people labelling data through its Hive Work app, and early on raised $30M+ from Peter Thiel's Founders Fund and others.
notes: Very low public profile; Kevin Guo is the public face. Input 'Hive' means Hive AI (thehive.ai), not Hive project-management software. Web search budget ran out before a deep-cut fact or press contact could be found; his current title is unverified.
